- Pale/cream kernels
- Prominent pink-to-reddish-purple discoloration between kernels
- Powdery/dusty growth in the center
- Pattern consistent with an ear rot

Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Gibberella** (pink/red mold), **Ear_rots_Fusarium** (white-pink scattered), **Ear_rots_Diplodia** (white mold). Let me view reference images.

The Gibberella reference shows stalk/leaf symptoms (not ear), Diplodia shows white powdery mold on ears, Fusarium shows white-pink scattered mold. The test image cross-section with pink-red discoloration is distinctive. Let me check more references.

Aspergillus = green mold, Trichoderma = blue-green, Common_smut = galls. None match. The test image (ear cross-section, pink-red discoloration) points to Gibberella ear rot. Let me verify with more comparisons.

None of the stalk rot images match the cross-section view with pink coloring. The test image is definitively an **ear cross-section** with pink-reddish-purple mold. Let me do a final check on a few more candidates.

I've now viewed 13 reference images. Summary of findings:
- **Head_smut**: dark powdery spore masses — no match
- **Gray_leaf_spot**: rectangular gray leaf lesions — no match  
- **Tar_spot**: tiny dark spots on leaves — no match

**Conclusion**: The test image is unambiguously a corn **ear cross-section** showing pale/cream kernels with characteristic **pink-to-reddish-purple mold** discoloration between the kernels. This is the hallmark presentation of **Gibberella ear rot** (*Fusarium graminearum*) — the pink/red coloration is pathognomonic for Gibberella vs. white (Diplodia), green (Aspergillus), or teal (Trichoderma) ear rots.
